title: The Lekki Headmaster
author: Kabir Alabi Garba
synopsis: The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba is a poignant, high-yield prose narrative prescribed for the JAMB UTME Use of English examination. Set in the high-brow maritime corridor of Lekki, Lagos State, at the prestigious Stardom Schools, the novel chronicles the professional, philosophical, and psychological trials of Mr. Adebepo Adewale (popularly known as "Bepo" or "The Lekki Headmaster"). A passionate educator of exceptional probity, Bepo finds himself trapped between unwavering devotion to mentoring Nigeria's future generation and the relentless societal and familial pressure to relocate abroad ("Japa"). Through emotional breakdowns, staff camaraderie, institutional power struggles, and profound introspective awakening, the text interrogates the socio-economic fault lines of contemporary Nigeria.

chapters.title: Dusk: The Morning Assembly Breakdown
chapters.summary:
At the morning assembly, Principal Bepo Adewale suddenly cannot talk.   

He walks to the podium looking sad and starts to cry in front of everyone.   

The Vice Principal (Mrs. Grace Apeh) and other staff try to find out what is wrong, but Bepo does not say anything.   

He is taken to his office, still weeping.   News of his strange behaviour reaches some parents and the Managing Director (MD), Mrs. Ibidun Gloss, is called to the school.   

She questions Bepo, but he only keeps saying, "I will be all right."   Even a pastor-teacher (Mr. Ope Wonde) is invited to talk to him too, but Bepo still will not explain his problem.   

The MD later learns that Bepo's wife now lives in London.   In the end, Bepo is asked to go home to rest.

chapters.title: The Enticement
chapters.summary:
We learn why Bepo was crying: he has decided to relocate (japa) to the United Kingdom.   

His wife (Seri) and their two children (Nike and Kike) are already in the UK, and Seri has been pressuring him to join them.   

But Bepo loves his job and his students at Stardom Schools, where he has worked for over 20 years and earned the nickname "The Lekki Headmaster".  

 His colleagues think he is foolish to be sad about such a "golden opportunity".   

People compare his Nigerian salary to what he could earn in pounds in the UK.   But Bepo had wanted to start his own transport or private school business when he retired.

chapters.title: Migration Tales
chapters.summary:
Bepo starts researching what life is like for Nigerians who have moved abroad.   

He learns about hourly wages in the UK, USA and Canada, and how much people can earn compared to Nigeria.   

He hears stories of Nigerians selling everything to relocate.   Some borrowing money and never paying back.   And even people who stole to fund their travel.   

His former colleague (Sola) who now lives in the UK, tells him about her experience — the good side like free healthcare and schools, and the opposite like low-paying jobs and expensive rent.   

Not every migration story is a success; some people abroad struggle badly

chapters.title: A Case of Visa Denied
chapters.summary:
A parent (Mrs. Ignatius) calls Bepo late at night to complain that her husband (Ibe) has not come home.   

Their family had planned to relocate to London, but their visa was denied because a DNA test showed that Mr. Ignatius is not the biological father of one of their three children.   

This discovery has caused serious trouble in the marriage, and Ibe threatens to leave his wife and the child who is not his.   

This chapter shows another side of the japa dream — how family secrets can be exposed by the visa process and how emigration is not always simple or happy.

chapters.title: Snake in the Roof
chapters.summary:
During lunch break, the MD (Mrs. Ibidun Gloss), goes to inspect a piece of land that the school owns.   

She is shocked to find many staff cars and big vehicles parked there secretly.   

She fears that teachers are stealing school money to buy these cars.   

She calls the accountant and principal to explain.   It turns out the money came from the school's staff cooperative society, which had grown very large — #95 million in the account, with #50 million loaned out.   

Worried that the cooperative has become too powerful (like "a snake in the roof"), the board of directors decides to limit how much any staff member can borrow, to protect the school from future risk.

chapters.title: Ade as well as Jide — COMES vs. COME
chapters.summary:
On the school's Open Day, a parent (Mr. Guta), is angry after reading a note by the English teacher (Mr. Fafore) that says "Ade as well as Jide comes early."   

The MD believes this is bad grammar and orders that Fafore be sacked immediately, without checking the fact first.   

Principal Bepo defends Fafore, explaining that the sentence is actually correct English grammar.   

Everyone checks online and finds that Bepo and Fafore are right, and the MD was wrong.   

The comic teacher (Mr. Audu) jokes about the matter and helps ease the embarrassment.   

Fafore is not sacked after all

chapters.title: Ritualists
chapters.summary:
This chapter looks back at Bepo's past.   He had worked at Beesway Group of Schools where he had a disagreement with the school director over a grammar mistake in the school's name.   

But the real reason he left Beesway was far more frightening – Bepo saw the director and some men trying to bury a cow alive on the school grounds late one night.   

When Bepo tried to stop them, he was attacked and injured.   

He also remembers an earlier experience when he and a friend ran a small school called Fruitful Future, where a parent offered to perform “magic” (using grains of corn) to attract more students — an offer Bepo refused.   

He later hears that that same man was arrested for murdering a woman using a similar ritual trick

chapters.title: Missions Unaccomplished
chapters.summary:
As Bepo prepares to leave Nigeria, he thinks about problems he has not yet solve at Stardom Schools.   

One big issue is a prolonged quarrel between two families of Banky and Tosh.   

It started from a dance competition and grew into political and legal conflict.   

During a school prefect election speech, Banky insults Tosh by calling his father “an ex-convict,” causing outrage.   

Bepo tried to make peace between the families, but the matter is still unresolved as he leaves.   

He is also sad about leaving the school's Invention Club, which was building a phone from recycled parts.   

But he vows to return for its launch if it succeeds.

chapters.title: Laughing Waterfalls
chapters.summary:
This chapter describes Stardom Schools' tradition of taking students on excursions around Nigeria.   

On their trip to Badagry (a town famous for its role in the transatlantic slave trade) students learn about the history of slavery, including the “Point of No Return”, where captured Africans were put on ships and taken away forever.   

Watching this history reminds Bepo of the modern “japa” trend.   And he sadly compares it to a “new form of slavery” — Nigerians rushing to leave their country for hard lives abroad, just as slaves were once forced away long ago.

chapters.title: Passport Pains
chapters.summary:
Bepo faces frustrating problems trying to renew his expired Nigerian passport.   

Because of large crowds and long delays at the Lagos passport office, he decides to travel to Ibadan for a faster process.   

On the journey, Bepo reflects on the changes he sees along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway — new roads, businesses and religious buildings.   

He ends up paying extra money to an agent (Tai) to speed things up, which shows how common bribery and "connection" are in government processes.   

Even after paying the agent, Bepo still faces more delays at the National Identity Number (NIN) office, which puts his travel date at risk

chapters.title: Point of No Return
chapters.summary:
The school organizes a big farewell party for Bepo.   

There are games, a debate, comedy skits mimicking Bepo's habits and traditional Nigerian dances, including a Canoe dance from Badagry.   

During the dance, Bepo becomes so emotional (remembering the slave history again) that he shouts out loud, disturbing the performance — but he quickly calms the crowd with a joke.   

The MD gives a moving speech praising Bepo's 24 years of service and presents him with a cheque of $10,000 as a farewell gift.   

Bepo is overcome with emotion and cries as he tries to give his thank-you speech.

chapters.title: Dawn: Return of the Master
chapters.summary:
Bepo prepares to travel to the UK, remembering an earlier time he missed a flight by misreading his ticket.   

This time, he is very careful.   His landlord's family comes to say goodbye, and his colleagues (the VP, accountant and other teachers) follow him to the airport.   

At the airport, Bepo checks in and later falls asleep while waiting to board.   

He has a frightening dream about the slave museum in Badagry, where he sees himself being forced onto a slave ship, and he wakes up screaming "Nooo!" just before the flight takes off.   

On the following Monday, students at Stardom Schools are sad that Bepo is gone — until, suddenly, he appears at the school gate!   

Bepo has decided not to leave Nigeria after all.   He tells everyone, "My heart is here!" and the students celebrate his return with joy.

characters.name: Mr. Adebepo Adewale ("Bepo")
characters.significance: The moral and narrative anchor of the novel. An erudite, compassionate, and uncompromising school administrator at Stardom Schools, Lekki. His internal tug-of-war between dedication to Nigerian youth and intense family pressure to emigrate (Japa) forms the core conflict. His refusal to board at MMIA epitomizes moral courage and patriotism.

characters.name: Mrs. Ibidun Gloss
characters.significance: An astute education businesswoman who recognizes that Bepo is the intellectual bedrock of the school. She offers financial incentives and administrative support, personifying enlightened educational entrepreneurship in urban Lagos.

characters.name: Mrs. Grace Apeh
characters.significance: Bepo’s dependable second-in-command who steps up to manage crises during his emotional breakdown. She represents steady administrative continuity and the dependable cadre of female educational leaders in Nigeria.

characters.name: Mrs. Beke Egbin
characters.significance: The empathetic voice of mental wellness in the staff room. She advocates for treating teachers’ psychological vulnerabilities and stresses that leaders also need therapeutic care.

characters.name: Mr. Wande
characters.significance: A charismatic, deeply spiritual educator who interprets institutional stress through theological and moral lenses. He provides spiritual encouragement to Bepo while sparking lively staff room debates on faith vs. economic reality.

characters.name: Mr. Alabi & Mr. Fafore
characters.significance: Pragmatic classroom teachers who vocalize the harsh economic realities of Lagos—inflation, fuel hikes, and high rents—grounding the novel in contemporary Nigerian socio-economic difficulties.

characters.name: Angel
characters.significance: Represents the student body. Her heartfelt testimonial during the Inter-House sports and her leadership during the peaceful student protest directly influence Bepo’s historic decision at the airport.

characters.name: Bepo’s Spouse & UK Relatives
characters.significance: The catalysts of Bepo’s crisis. Living abroad in the UK, they view remaining in Nigeria as foolishness and relentlessly urge him to abandon Stardom Schools for Western opportunities.
